items.title: Pai
items.subtitle: Town in Thailand
items.description: Pai is a town in the Mae Hong Soon Province of northern Thailand. It sits in a valley on the banks of the Pai River. It's known for its nearby gorges, hot springs like the Tha Pai Hot Spring and waterfalls like Mo Paeng Waterfall. Downtown, food stalls and handicraft shops line Pai Walking Street. West of town lies Baan Santichon, a traditional Chinese village with clay houses and eateries serving Yunnan cuisine. ― Google

items.text: Pai is a town in the Mae Hong Soon Province of northern Thailand. It sits in a valley on the banks of the Pai River. It's known for its nearby gorges, hot springs like the Tha Pai Hot Spring and waterfalls like Mo Paeng Waterfall. Downtown, food stalls and handicraft shops line Pai Walking Street. West of town lies Baan Santichon, a traditional Chinese village with clay houses and eateries serving Yunnan cuisine. ― Google

items.markdown:
![THE 10 BEST Things to Do in Pai (2026) - Must-See Attractions](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07270019-1672-0139-0000-d5fbc333ded7:8)
Pai is `a relaxed mountain town in northern Thailand known for its scenic valleys, hot springs, and vibrant hippie culture` . Located about 146 km northwest of Chiang Mai, it is famous for the winding road of 762 curves required to reach it.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pai,_Thailand) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pai,_Thailand)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zpxUZpdD_gQ)[[3]](https://www.theblondtravels.com/places-see-pai)[[4]](https://www.skyetravels.com/guide-to-pai/)

Top Attractions

- **Pai Canyon:** Narrow ridges offering dramatic sunset views over the jungle canopy.
- **Wat Phra That Mae Yen:** A massive white Buddha statue on a hill overlooking the valley.
- **Hot Springs & Waterfalls:** Popular spots include Tha Pai Hot Spring, Sai Ngam Hot Spring, and Mo Paeng Waterfall.
- **Pai Walking Street:** A bustling night market featuring street food, local crafts, and live music.[](https://www.skyetravels.com/guide-to-pai/) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o_-CuMyTUV4&t=14)[[2]](https://www.thelostpassport.com/pai-thailand-guide/)[[3]](https://www.pm-tours.com/pm-tours-blog/everything-you-need-to-know-about-pai)

Travel and Tips

- **Getting There:** A 3 to 3.5-hour minivan ride from Chiang Mai costs roughly 150 to 250 baht, or you can rent a scooter if you are an experienced rider.[](https://inbetweentravels.com/pai-travel-guide-thailand/) [[1]](https://inbetweentravels.com/pai-travel-guide-thailand/)
- **Best Time to Visit:** November to February offers cool, dry weather, whereas March to May brings heavy smoke from agricultural burning (the burning season).[](https://inbetweentravels.com/pai-travel-guide-thailand/)
